blocks.title: Your computers, reachable from each other
blocks.description: Two directions in one panel: this machine as something you can log in to from a phone or another computer, and your other computers as places you can drive from here. The device code, the autostart switch that unattended access depends on, and the channel state are all on the first screen.

showcase.user_prompt: I'm at the office. Can I get into the desktop at home and start a build?
showcase.assistant_reply: Home desktop is online — I can see it in your ToDesk account. I've asked ToDesk to open the session; accept it in the client window. Once you're in, tell me which folder and I'll fire the build through the agent.

items.title: Get in from a phone or a PC
items.description: The inbound card gives the two real paths: install the app and type the device code, or sign in on another computer and pick this machine from 设备列表.

items.title: Drive your other computers
items.description: When the channel is open the panel lists the devices in your account with their live status and connects in one press — ToDesk hands back a link and the client takes it.

items.title: Works with the channel closed
items.description: ToDesk's documented command line connects by device code and password, so the panel stays useful before the MCP switch is on.

items.title: Unattended, checked not assumed
items.description: Sign-in, a security password, start-with-Windows and no system sleep — the four things remote access to a home machine actually needs, with the autostart switch as a button.

items.title: Identity from ToDesk itself
items.description: The device code and version are read from ToDesk's own status command, with its config file as a fallback — no invented numbers, ever.

items.title: Dangerous tools fenced off
items.description: Remote shell execution and screen lock/unlock are blocked by default; screenshots, files, sessions and pointer control stay available.

items.title: Install and sign in to ToDesk on this computer
items.description: The plugin does not ship or install ToDesk; it drives the copy you already use.

items.title: Make it reachable while you are away
items.description: Set a security password, turn on start-with-Windows from the panel, and disable system sleep.

items.title: Turn on ToDesk's local MCP server
items.description: In ToDesk's AI / MCP settings. The panel probes 127.0.0.1:8899 and says “open” once it answers; paste the token if it asks for one.

items.title: Connect in whichever direction you need
items.description: Inbound: device code plus password from the other side. Outbound: pick a device from the account list, or type its code in the manual field.

blocks.content: The panel shows the device code, never a password. Temporary passwords rotate and live in ToDesk's own window; security passwords stay in ToDesk's settings. Copying either into a chat transcript would be a downgrade.

The account device list and the one-press connect need ToDesk's MCP channel, which ships closed. With the channel off the panel falls back to ToDesk's documented `-control` command, which only works for devices already unlocked in your device list.
